STEP 1 - Scene: A light breakfast/snack tray: a mug of black tea (or similar hot drink), two slices of toast on a plate, and two jam packets (strawberry).

STEP 2 - Vessel: Paper/disposable plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) two slices of toast (bread, lightly browned, appears wholemeal/multigrain), (b) strawberry jam packets (2 small sachets, actually on the tray beside the mug, not on the plate).

STEP 4 - Area: Toast covers roughly 25% of the plate area (two overlapping slices, about 130 cm^2 combined footprint). Jam packets are not on the plate, so they are excluded from the plate area calculation.

STEP 5 - Volume: Toast 130 cm^2 x ~1.5 cm (two slices stacked/overlapping, outer envelope) ≈ 195 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 195 ml x 0.3 g/ml (bread-like, toast is airy; the bread loaf value is the applicable density) ≈ 60 g. Two slices of sandwich bread typically weigh about 60–70 g, so 60 g is consistent.

STEP 7 - Energy: Toast ~260 kcal/100 g (wholemeal toast, dry-ish) x 60 g ≈ 156 kcal. Strawberry jam sachets, ~15 g each (about 2 x 15 g = 30 g) at ~250 kcal/100 g ≈ 75 kcal. Tea with no milk or sugar is ~0 kcal (mug not counted as food). The jam is on the tray, so I include it as a visible item in the meal, though it is not on the plate.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two toast slices (~60 g, ~155 kcal) plus two jam sachets (~30 g, ~75 kcal) is plausible for what is visible. Total ≈ 90 g, ~230 kcal.
